2609.23876.title: GLR-MM: Graph-Based Global-Local Reconstruction for Robust Multimodal Chest X-ray and EHR Representation Learning under Missing Modalities
2609.23876.paper_summary: Clinical multimodal models must often predict before all chest X-ray (CXR) and electronic health record (EHR) inputs are available. Existing approaches align observed representations, model missingness, or reconstruct across modalities, but do not jointly exploit within-patient and clinically similar inter-patient evidence. We propose GLR-MM, a Graph-Based Global-Local Reconstruction framework for early ICU mortality prediction. It maps five CXR-EHR modalities to a shared space, reconstructs missing embeddings through complementary local cross-modal and global graph-attention branches, adaptively fuses their estimates, and optimizes class-balanced prediction, reconstruction, and contrastive objectives. On 9,620 MIMIC-derived ICU stays, we evaluate 10%, 30%, and 50% random modality missingness with shared deterministic masks. MUSE performs better under mild and moderate missingness, whereas GLR-MM achieves higher AUROC and AUPRC at 50% by 0.0088 and 0.0249, respectively. These results indicate that graph-guided reconstruction is most useful when inputs are severely incomplete.
2609.23876.paper_summary_zh: 臨床多模態模型往往必須在所有胸部X光（CXR）和電子健康記錄（EHR）輸入可用之前進行預測。現有的方法對觀察到的表示進行對齊，建模缺失性，或在不同模態之間重建，但未能共同利用患者內部和臨床相似的患者間證據。我們提出了GLR-MM，一個基於圖形的全局-局部重建框架，用於早期ICU死亡率預測。它將五種CXR-EHR模態映射到共享空間，通過互補的局部跨模態和全局圖形注意分支重建缺失的嵌入，自適應融合它們的估計，並優化類別平衡的預測、重建和對比目標。在9,620個MIMIC衍生的ICU住院期間，我們評估了10%、30%和50%的隨機模態缺失性，並使用共享的確定性掩碼。在輕度和中度缺失性下，MUSE的表現更佳，而GLR-MM在50%的情況下分別提高了0.0088和0.0249的AUROC和AUPRC。這些結果表明，圖形引導的重建在輸入嚴重不完整時最為有用。
